authorization: Main explicitly authorized the isolated us-west-2 recorder/channel lifecycle through AWSConfig after read-only verification that the region had no recorder or delivery channel.
method: Actual boto3 AWS API calls and AWS CLI read-only checks. No fabricated response fixtures. SDK response metadata/request IDs are retained; credential fields and SQS receipt handles are not retained.
capture_notes: The original background probe queried SQS history using an ARN, then encountered empty unbounded history pages. Actual Config SQS resource IDs are queue URLs; bounded earlierTime/laterTime queries returned the native items. The probe source now uses the observed identifiers and time range.

After recording reached SUCCESS, exact-owned queue and bucket tags were changed. Native ResourceDiscovered observations arrived approximately 17 minutes after initial recorder start. The capture does not claim a fixed AWS discovery latency.

The exact-owned recorder role's inline policy was expanded using documented AWS_ConfigRole discovery/read prerequisites. The capture does not establish that these additions caused discovery; the original policy and changed policy are both retained.

Supplemental native calls continued the original exact-owned resources through visibility/tag/versioning changes, deletion, retained history and a final snapshot. The original background process was interrupted after this continuation; its finally cleanup ran. Its recorder deletion was throttled, then completed successfully in the separate cleanup capture.
Native zero-width history ranges returned no items, while nonzero ranges containing either exact endpoint included the item. Inverted bounds returned InvalidTimeRangeException.
SQS numeric and boolean configuration attributes are JSON strings in the native history item, despite the searchable resource schema's numeric property declarations.

No new user, access key, service-linked role, KMS key, baseline recorder, baseline channel, or unrelated resource was created or modified. The Config service's retained observation history remains AWS-managed after resource deletion.
